en: The Sūtra Spoken by the Buddha on the Questions of the Upāsaka Viśuddhamati,
translated by the Tripitaka Master of the Western Heaven, the Court-Attendant Grand Officer,
Acting Director of the Court of Imperial Entertainments, Great Master of the Transmission of the Dharma, and Recipient of the Purple Robe.
Translated by the Subject Shi Hu, by Imperial Decree: Thus have I heard:
At one time, the Buddha was staying in Śrāvastī at the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍada’s Park, together with a great assembly.
At that time, there was a son of a noble family in the city named Śuddhamati, who approached the place where the Buddha was.

Having arrived at the Buddha’s presence, he beheld the Buddha’s marks and signs of excellence; his heart was filled with joy, and he offered various praises. Joining his palms in reverence and prostrating at the Buddha’s feet, he withdrew to stand to one side.
At that time, Viśuddhamati, son of Tuṇḍila, stepped forward and addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
I have a minor matter regarding the Dharma that I wish to inquire about; I pray that the Buddha, the World-Honored One, will grant me permission to speak.”
The Buddha said, “Viśuddhamati! Whatever doubts you may have, ask now as you please; the Buddha shall resolve each one for you.”
At that time, Viśuddhamati, son of Tuṇḍila, addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
I observe all the multitudes of people in the world, each distinguished by various modes of conduct; I see some who attain long life and others who have short lives.”
There are those with many illnesses and those with few illnesses;
there are those who are handsome and those who are ugly;
there are those whose wishes are fulfilled and those whose wishes are not fulfilled.
There are those born into low castes and those born into high castes;
there are the wealthy and noble, and the poor;
there are the foolish and the wise—such are the various distinctions among these classes of beings.
"By what causes and conditions does such retribution arise?
I pray that the Buddha, the World-Honored One, will explain this for me.
The Buddha said:
“Viśuddhamati! You should now know that because the causal actions performed by sentient beings in the world differ, the fruits they obtain are each distinct.”
Then, Viśuddhamati, son of Tuṇḍila, again addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
Regarding the distinctions between cause and effect as spoken of by the Buddha, we pray that the Buddha, the World-Honored One, will provide a brief exposition, or perhaps a detailed explanation.”
"I am unable to understand this meaning," [he said].
The Buddha said, "Viśuddhamati!"
“You should listen attentively and apply your minds well; I shall now speak for you.
At that time, Viśuddhamati, son of Dronya, received the instruction and listened.
The Buddha said:

“Viśuddhamati! You should now know that there are certain men and women in the world whose hearts harbor foul venom; they may at times carry knives or wield staves, seeking out opportunities to kill living beings. Lacking any heart of compassion and feeling no shame or remorse, they either kill with their own hands or incite others to kill.”
Due to these causes and conditions, at the dissolution of the body after death, they fall into the evil realms and undergo the sufferings of hell.
When their retribution in hell is exhausted and they happen to obtain human birth, in every place where they are born, their lifespan is short.
"Śuddhamati, you should know that due to the cause of killing living beings, one obtains the fruit of a short lifespan. Furthermore, Śuddhamati!
There are certain men and women in the world whose minds are free from malice; they do not carry swords or staves, nor do they kill living beings, but possess a heart of compassion and great shame."
By virtue of these causes and conditions, at the dissolution of the body and the end of life, they will be reborn in a happy destination, receiving a celestial or human body.
When their retribution in the heavens is exhausted and they are born again among humans, wherever they are born, their lifespan will be long and enduring.
"Śuddhamati, you should know that by the cause of not killing, one realizes the fruit of long life. Furthermore, Śuddhamati!

There are certain men and women in the world who, at times, take up sticks, clubs, tiles, or stones to strike or hurl at sentient beings, or otherwise personally inflict harm and distress upon others."
Due to these causes and conditions, at the dissolution of the body and the end of life, they fall into the evil realms and undergo the sufferings of hell.
When their retribution in hell is exhausted and they happen to obtain human birth, they will suffer from many diseases wherever they are born.
"Śuddhamati, you should know that due to the cause of malice and harm, one experiences the fruit of much illness.

Furthermore, Śuddhamati, there are certain men and women in the world who do not strike or hurl at sentient beings with sticks, wood, tiles, or stones, nor do they afflict others with their own hands."
By virtue of these causes and conditions, at the dissolution of the body and the end of life, they will be reborn in a happy destination, receiving a celestial or human body.
When their retribution in the heavens is exhausted and they are born again among humans, they will suffer little illness wherever they are born.
"Śuddhamati, you should know that by reason of not causing harm or affliction, one brings about the fruit of having few ailments. Furthermore, Śuddhamati!
There are certain men and women in the world who constantly give rise to a mind of resentment, hatred, and anger, thereby producing various faults."
Due to these causes and conditions, at the dissolution of the body after death, they fall into the evil realms and undergo the sufferings of hell.
When their retribution in hell is exhausted and they happen to obtain a human birth, they will be of ugly appearance wherever they are born.
"Śuddhamati, you should know that due to the cause of anger and resentment, one experiences the fruit of ugliness. Furthermore, Śuddhamati!
There are certain men and women in the world who do not give rise to thoughts of anger, malice, or hatred, and thus do not produce faults."
By virtue of these causes and conditions, at the dissolution of the body and the end of life, they will be reborn in a happy destination, receiving the form of a deva or a human.
When their retribution in the heavens is exhausted and they are born again among humans, they will possess handsome and upright features wherever they are born.
"Śuddhamati, you should know that by reason of not being prone to anger, one brings about the fruit of physical beauty. Furthermore, Śuddhamati!

There are certain men and women in the world who, upon seeing others obtain gains, offerings, or even fame and other pleasing things, employ various means to create obstacles so that others do not receive them."
Due to these causes and conditions, at the dissolution of the body and the end of life, they fall into the evil realms and undergo the sufferings of hell.
When their retribution in hell is exhausted and they happen to obtain human form, in every place where they are born, whatever they undertake will not accord with their wishes.
"Śuddhamati, you should know that due to the cause of obstructing things that are pleasing to others, one experiences results that are not as desired. Furthermore, Śuddhamati!

There are certain men and women in the world who, upon seeing the gains, honors, or even the fame and other pleasing things belonging to others, do not employ means to create obstacles, but rather desire that others obtain them."
By virtue of these causes and conditions, at the dissolution of the body and the end of life, one will be reborn in a happy destination, receiving a celestial or human body.
When the retribution in the heavens is exhausted and one is born again among humans, in every place of birth and in all that one undertakes, everything will be accomplished according to one's wishes.
"Śuddhamati, you should know that by not obstructing the causes of others' pleasing matters, one brings about results that accord with one's wishes. Furthermore, Śuddhamati!

There are certain men and women in the world who do not respect those whom they ought to respect, do not honor those whom they ought to honor, and do not make offerings to those whom they ought to offer to; they constantly give rise to pride and exalt their own minds."
Due to these causes and conditions, at the dissolution of the body and the end of life, they fall into the evil realms and undergo the sufferings of hell.
When their retribution in hell is exhausted and they happen to obtain human form, in every place where they are born, they always descend into lowly families.
"Vimalamati, you should know that by taking the arising of self-conceit and self-exaltation as a cause, one brings about the fruit of birth in a lowly family. Furthermore, Vimalamati,

there are certain men and women in the world who show respect toward those who deserve respect, show reverence toward those who deserve reverence, and provide offerings to those who deserve offerings, without giving rise to a mind of self-conceit and self-exaltation."
By virtue of these causes and conditions, at the dissolution of the body and the end of life, they will be reborn in a happy realm, receiving a celestial or human body.
When their retribution in the heavens is exhausted and they are born again among humans, in every place where they are born, they will always be born into a noble family.
"Śuddhamati, you should know that by not giving rise to the conceit of self-exaltation as a cause, one brings about the fruit of birth in a noble family. Furthermore, Śuddhamati!

There are certain men and women in the world whose minds are stingy; they do not give food, drink, clothing, bedding, medicine, dwellings, or seats, nor even unguents and powdered incense, to śramaṇas, brāhmaṇas, and others."
Due to these causes and conditions, at the dissolution of the body and the end of life, they fall into the evil realms and undergo the sufferings of hell.
Once their retribution in hell is exhausted and they happen to obtain human birth, they will be impoverished and destitute wherever they are born.
"Vimalamati, you should know that through the cause of stinginess, one experiences the fruit of poverty. Furthermore, Vimalamati!

There are certain men and women in the world whose minds are not stingy; they constantly give food, drink, clothing, bedding, medicine, dwellings, seats, and even ointments and powdered incense to śramaṇas, brahmins, and others."
By virtue of these causes and conditions, at the dissolution of the body and the end of life, they will be reborn in a happy destination, receiving a celestial or human body.
When their retribution in the heavens is exhausted and they return to birth in the human realm, wherever they are born, they will possess wealth, nobility, and sovereignty.
"Viśuddhamati, you should know that through the cause of non-avarice, one experiences the fruit of wealth and nobility.

Furthermore, Viśuddhamati! There are certain men and women in the world whose minds do not delight in the sūtras of the True Dharma, nor do they inquire about various meanings from śramaṇas or brāhmaṇas."
What is wholesome? What is unwholesome?
What should be initiated?
What should not be initiated?
What should be practiced?
And what should not be practiced?
Being unable to inquire in this manner for clarification and resolution,
they will, due to these causes and conditions, fall into the evil realms at the dissolution of the body after death and undergo the sufferings of hell.
Once their retribution in hell is exhausted and they happen to obtain a human birth, they will be born in every place as foolish and lacking in wisdom.
"Vimalamanas, you should know that by not delighting in the Dharma and not inquiring about the causes of the Dharma, one brings about the fruit of delusion.
Furthermore, Vimalamanas!

There are certain men and women in the world whose minds constantly love and delight in the sūtras of the True Dharma, and who are further able to inquire about various meanings from śramaṇas and brāhmaṇas."
What is wholesome? What is unwholesome?
What should be initiated?
What should not be initiated?
What should be practiced?
And what should not be practiced?
Being able to inquire and seek clarification in this manner,
by virtue of these causes and conditions, at the dissolution of the body and the end of life, one will be reborn in a happy realm, receiving a celestial or human body.
When the retribution in the heavens is exhausted and one is born again in the human world, wherever one is born, one will possess great wisdom.
"Vimalamati, you should know that through the causes of delighting in the Dharma and inquiring about the Dharma,
the fruit of wisdom is realized. Furthermore,
Vimalamati, such are the various distinctions between cause and effect as I have explained above."
Therefore, one should know that the cause of a short life results in the fruit of a short life, and the cause of a long life results in the fruit of a long life;
the cause of much illness results in the fruit of much illness, and the cause of little illness results in the fruit of little illness;
the cause of ugliness results in the fruit of ugliness, and the cause of physical excellence results in the fruit of physical excellence.
From causes that are unfavorable, one obtains unfavorable results; from causes that are favorable, one obtains favorable results.
From causes of low birth, one obtains the result of low birth; from causes of high birth, one obtains the result of high birth.
From causes of poverty, one obtains the result of poverty; from causes of wealth and honor, one obtains the result of wealth and honor.
Through the cause of delusion one obtains the fruit of delusion; through the cause of wisdom one obtains the fruit of wisdom.
O Pure-Minded One!

Therefore, you should now understand as it truly is: that the causes and conditions for short life are taught by the Buddha; the causes and conditions for long life are taught by the Buddha; the causes and conditions for much illness are taught by the Buddha; the causes and conditions for little illness are taught by the Buddha; the causes and conditions for ugliness are taught by the Buddha; the causes and conditions for physical beauty are taught by the Buddha; the causes and conditions for what is disagreeable are taught by the Buddha; the causes and conditions for what is agreeable are taught by the Buddha; the causes and conditions for low birth are taught by the Buddha; the causes and conditions for high birth are taught by the Buddha; the causes and conditions for poverty are taught by the Buddha; the causes and conditions for wealth and honor are taught by the Buddha; the causes and conditions for folly are taught by the Buddha; and the causes and conditions for wisdom are taught by the Buddha. For this reason, the wise act according to these teachings.

“Śuddhamati, you should know that the Buddha has declared long life to be a supreme reward for wholesome karma; freedom from illness to be a supreme reward for wholesome karma; physical beauty to be a supreme reward for wholesome karma; fulfillment of one’s wishes to be a supreme reward for wholesome karma; birth into a noble family to be a supreme reward for wholesome karma; wealth and status to be a supreme reward for wholesome karma; and wisdom to be a supreme reward for wholesome karma.”
"Viśuddhamati!
Such dharmas as these have been taught by the Buddha; you should practice and study them.
At that time, having heard this Dharma, Viśuddhamati, son of a Tuṇeya, felt great joy in his heart and addressed the Buddha, saying:
“World-Honored One!
It is like the various dark places in the world where one cannot discern the path to be traveled; although one possesses eyes, one is unable to see clearly.”
If there is a wise person who holds a torch, they will be able to traverse all the paths they travel.
The World-Honored One is likewise; by skillfully expounding the True Dharma, he destroys all ignorance and is able to discern each and every phenomenon with complete clarity.
"This is wholesome; this is unwholesome;
this should be initiated; this should not be initiated;
this is what should be practiced; this is what should not be practiced."
Such dharmas as these can only be skillfully proclaimed by a Buddha, a Tathāgata, an Arhat, a Samyaksaṃbuddha, appearing in the world.

Today I have swiftly attained great benefit; I now take refuge in the Buddha, take refuge in the Dharma, and take refuge in the Saṅgha of Bhikṣus. Upholding the precepts such as non-killing, I become a lay follower (upāsaka).
"I pray that the Buddha, the World-Honored One,
will accept me. The Buddha said, "Excellent!"
"I now accept you.
Then, the upāsaka Viśuddhamati addressed the Buddha, saying:
"World-Honored One!"
Now, if the sons of noble families within this city of Śrāvastī were to hear of this matter, they would all surely think to themselves:
"The son of Tuṇḍila has, throughout the long night, skillfully brought benefit to sentient beings and guided them."
When the upāsaka Viśuddhamati had spoken these words, he prostrated to the Buddha and withdrew.
This concludes the *Sūtra on the Questions of the Upāsaka Viśuddhamati* as taught by the Buddha.
